# **PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS**

## 🎮 **My Experience**

PUBG is honestly one of the games I keep coming back to. The idea is simple: land, loot, survive, and be the last one standing. But somehow, every match turns into a completely different experience.

Sometimes you land in a busy place and immediately start fighting. Other times, you spend 10 minutes just looking for a decent gun, only to get shot by someone hiding in a random building. 😂

## 🔫 **The Gunplay**

I really like the gunplay in PUBG. The guns feel different, and you actually have to practice if you want to get better. You can't just run around shooting everything and expect to win.

There are times when you hit a really nice shot and feel like a pro, then the next game you can't hit anything. **That's just PUBG.**

## 👥 **Playing With Friends**

PUBG is way more fun with friends. Playing squads, talking on voice chat, making stupid decisions together, and somehow surviving makes the game really enjoyable.

The best moments are when your whole team is almost dead, you have barely any supplies left, and somehow you still manage to win the fight.

Of course, sometimes your friends are also the reason you lose. 😂

*"Don't worry, I got you!"*

**Dies 5 seconds later.**

## 🗺️ **The Maps**

I like that there are different maps to play, so the game doesn't always feel the same. You can choose to land somewhere crowded if you want action or go somewhere quieter and take your time.

The map also plays a big part in the game. Sometimes you have a great position, and sometimes the safe zone decides to spawn on the complete opposite side of the map. 😭

## 😭 **The Bad Part**

PUBG can definitely be frustrating.

You can spend a lot of time looting, get good weapons and equipment, survive several fights, and then suddenly get eliminated by someone you didn't even see.

And when you finally reach the top 10, your heart starts beating like you're playing for a million dollars.

Then you get killed.

Back to the lobby.

**"One more game."**

## 🏆 **Final Thoughts**

Overall, PUBG is a really fun battle royale, especially when playing with friends. It can be frustrating sometimes, but that's also part of what makes the good moments feel so much better.

Getting a Chicken Dinner after a long and difficult match is still one of the best feelings in the game.

**Would recommend.**

2300 hours, and I’m done.

I’ve played this game for over 2,300 hours, and it genuinely hurts to see what it has become.

Ranked has become increasingly difficult to take seriously because of the amount of blatant cheating. This isn’t just “closet cheating” anymore. You regularly encounter players using Aimbot, ESP/Wallhack, aim-lock, no-recoil scripts, and other obvious cheats.

I’ve seen players tracking enemies through terrain, snapping onto targets with Aimbot, landing completely unnatural long-range spray transfers, and even using Aimbot while driving at full speed.

You can spend 10 minutes rotating, positioning, and making smart decisions, only to have the entire squad instantly deleted by someone who isn't actually playing the same game.

And the punishment system makes the situation even more frustrating.

You get a notification saying a cheater was banned, but what does that actually accomplish when they can simply purchase another cheap recycled account and return to ranked almost immediately?

The legitimate players lose their RP, time, and motivation, while the cheater loses an account that costs almost nothing to replace.

That isn't an effective deterrent.

Meanwhile, KRAFTON continues releasing expensive skins and progressive gachas while the core competitive experience is being damaged by cheating.

I don't expect a perfect anti-cheat system. I understand that cheat developers will always try to stay ahead.

What I expect is a serious effort to protect the legitimate player base.

Detect cheaters faster. Make repeat offenders harder to return. Improve the ban system. And most importantly, stop making legitimate players pay the price for matches ruined by confirmed cheaters.

After 2,300 hours, this isn't a review from someone who simply hates the game.

It's a review from someone who wanted this game to succeed.

But right now, ranked feels less and less like a competitive shooter and more like a battle between legitimate players and whoever has the better cheat.

KRAFTON, fix the anti-cheat. Before you lose the players who actually kept this game alive.
